machatzit_hashekel.en: (סק ג) One garment, etc.—even with his belt it is permitted, even for us. Meaning in Moed Katan 14a R' Yochanan permits one who has only one garment to launder it on the festival; they challenge that the matter is not evident and there is concern for marit ayin. They answer: Mar bar Rav Ashi—his belt proves it; likewise in Chullin. Rashi in Chullin: the belt is always fixed to the garment; when he removes the garment and wears another he takes the belt from this and fixes it on that; and one who has no other garment launders with the belt, and the viewer seeing him launder with the belt knows he has no other garment. However for our garments where the belt is not fixed it is forbidden; rather we hold like Rashi in the first chapter on “his belt proves it”—when one has only one garment, when he removes it to launder he wraps himself in his cloak and girds the belt on the cloak; thereby everyone knows when he launders he has only one garment, for they see the belt girded on his cloak; therefore for us too it is permitted. But the Rabbenu Yerucham wrote that according to this explanation it would be forbidden for one person to launder even his wife's garment, for if another launders and one does not see the belt on the cloak there is marit ayin; also if one lends a garment only until after laundering he is not girding the belt on the cloak—also it should be forbidden; but since both are uncommon—for typically one with only one garment has no one to use it and must launder himself, and it is uncommon that one lends a garment only until after laundering and no more—it was permitted in all cases, even if another lends a garment after laundering or another launders and it is not he himself, since it is uncommon the rabbis were lenient.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ה) מותר כו' ולא עיין במרדכי כו' במשפט הגוים כו' ר"ל דבחה"מ מיירי בדין ישראל שהבע"ד ישראל וגם הדיינים ישראלים. ובניסן ותשרי דטרודים בטרדת המועד לא אטרחוהו לא לבע"ד ולא לב"ד משא"כ המרדכי מיירי שהבע"ד גוי. וגם בעל המשפט הוא גוי ובס' א"ר כ' וז"ל ולא דק דסמ"ע לא הקשה אהכא כלל. רק על ס"ס תקמ"ה דמיירי לקבול בב"הכ עכ"ל. ובעניתי לא ידעתי למה כ' עליו ולא דק ניהו דבס"ס תקמ"ה כ' הרב"י מותר לקבול בשביל חובותיו כו' ולא הגיה עליו רמ"א. ניהו דהמחבר לא כ' תיבת במשפט. כ"ח לקבול ויש לפרש דר"ל בב"הכ מ"מ לא רצה רמ"א להשיג כיון די"ל ר"ל במשפט ואיירי במשפט עכו"ם דהא גם דינו של הרב"י לקמן ס"ס תקמ"ה נובע מדברי המרדכי הנ"ל שהגהת רמ"א פה נובע ממנה. ודא ודא אחת היא. וממ"ש הרב"י שם לעיל מיניה דנין בין ד"מ ובין ד"נ כו' יש לומר דמיירי ברצון שני בע"ד וברצון ב"ד. וקמ"ל אף דבשבת וי"ט אין דנים משום גזרה שמא יכתוב בחה"מ שרי וגם בד"נ משכחת רצון שניהם. כגון שהנתבע רוצח וכה"ג מדמה בנפשו שיצא זכאי בדינו. וחפץ בזה שימהרו להוציא זכותו לאור. גם בלא"ה יש לומר דיני נפשות שאני. ומ"ש משמתין ומכין למי שלא מקבל הדין הטעם כיון שכבר דנו בהיתר או קודם י"ט או בחה"מ:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (sk 5) Permitted, etc. — and he did not look in Mordechai, etc. in judgment of gentiles, etc. — meaning in Chol HaMoed it deals with judgment of Israel where the plaintiff is Israelite and the judges too are Israelites; and in Nisan and Tishrei, when they are busy with the bustle of the festival, they did not trouble him — neither the plaintiff nor the court — unlike Mordechai, which deals where the plaintiff is a gentile and the litigant in the case is also a gentile; and in Sefer Ateret Roshei he wrote: and he was not precise — Semak did not challenge here at all, only on the end of siman 545 that it deals with receiving in court of appeals — end quote; and in my answer I did not know why he wrote on him "and he was not precise" — for at the end of siman 545 Rabbeinu Yehudah wrote it is permitted to receive for his debts, etc., and the Rama did not emend on him — meaning the Mechaber did not write the word "in judgment," only "to receive"; and one could explain he means in court of appeals; nevertheless the Rama did not wish to challenge, since one could explain he means in judgment of gentiles — for Rabbeinu Yehudah's law below at the end of siman 545 also derives from this Mordechai that Rama's gloss here derives from it; and surely surely it is one. And from what Rabbeinu Yehudah wrote there earlier that they judge both monetary and capital cases, etc. — one could say it deals with the will of both plaintiff and court; and it teaches that although on Shabbat and Yom Tov they do not judge because of a decree lest one write — on Chol HaMoed it is permitted; and also in capital cases one finds the will of both — such as when the defendant is a murderer and imagines in his soul he will be acquitted in his judgment and desires that they hurry to bring his acquittal to light; also in any case one could say capital laws are different. And what he wrote "they excommunicate and strike one who does not accept the judgment" — the reason: since they already judged when permitted, either before Yom Tov or on Chol HaMoed.

turei_zahav.en: They do not fine his son after him. Beit Yosef writes: Rabbenu Yerucham in the name of the commentators that they do not fine his son after him specifically for davar ha-aved, but for what is not davar ha-aved if he did it on chol ha-moed they remove it from him and even if dead they fine his son after him; it appears this is for the view that melacha on chol ha-moed is biblical, therefore for what is not davar ha-aved they fine his son after him as we say regarding a kohen who squeezed a firstborn's ear and they fined his son after him since it is forbidden biblically, until here. It is fitting to consider that Rabbenu Yerucham is not carried by the commentators on such a matter in the Talmud; as it appears he intended well as it is in the Gemara, chapter “What are,” R' Yehudah asked R' Zeira: intentional melacha on the festival and he died—do they fine his son after him? They suggested: one who squeezes a firstborn's ear—they fine his son after him because he did a prohibition; but intentional melacha he had not yet done a prohibition (thus the text). He answered: you learned it, etc.—the pit was good and he died, his son sowed it—apparently for his view they fine the son, the rabbis do not fine the son; likewise for his view they fine, etc. In chapter 25, 44a they also ask, etc., and rule like here. The commentators hold that for intentional melacha on the festival for what is not davar ha-aved and he did melacha, what is the law regarding fining his son—they need not ask on squeezing a firstborn's ear which is anyway biblical; rather this question should be asked where this question is asked; certainly for this it is simple to fine also the son, for there are two adverse factors: one that he intends melacha for chol ha-moed, second that he actually does what is not davar ha-aved; if so here too per the conclusion in “one who plants in the Sabbatical year” there is only one adverse factor that he did a prohibition, but with two prohibitions certainly they fine; and per these words I reconcile also on Ri'ban who wrote the commentators hold melacha on chol ha-moed is biblical from equating to squeezing the ear and hold even per the conclusion here they fine the son since there are two adverse factors—the view of Ri'ban in the name of the commentators is correct.

וכו' אלא לצורך המועד ולא חילקה דמעכו"ם שרי וכן בש"ס לא הביאה לתוספתא זו לחלק בזה אלמא דלא ס"ל להלכה וביותר דהמשנה פרטה אלא לצורך המועד או לצורך המוכר אלמא דאין לנו עוד אופן היתר. ועוד אפשר לומר דהרמב"ם וש"פ שלא כתבו היתר זו מבארים התוספתא בפירוש אחר מהש"ג דהתוספתא לא באת לחדש דמעכו"ם שרי טפי מישראל ורק דמעכו"ם נמי שרי ומיירי נמי לצורך המועד דוקא ולא הצריכה לבאר זאת דקאי על המשנה והוסיפה רק זאת דמעכו"ם נמי שרי אף דדברים אלו צריך לכתוב ולהעלות בערכאות אפ"ה מותר דכיון דהלקיחה מותר לצורך המועד הכתיבה והערכאות נמי שרי משום שהוא כמציל מידם [וכנ"ל מרש"י והה"מ] [ולולא דמסתפינא הייתי אומר עוד דהתוספתא לא קאי כלל לענין מועד דכל לשון התוספתא נשנית בע"ז דף י"ג ובעירובין דף מ"ז לענין הולכין ליריד של עכו"ם וחסר כאן רק אלו התיבות הולכין ליריד של עכו"ם ולוקחין וכו'. ונשנית כאן דטעם התירא הוא. biur_halacha.en:
(א) One does not buy, etc. — see Mishna Berurah what he wrote that from a gentile some say it is permitted to buy houses, fields, and vineyards, etc., because it is like saving from their hand; so Shach in the name of Tosefta, and Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah brought it. And what he wrote the reason "because it is like saving from their hand" is not agreed upon by the poskim in my humble opinion, for in the Tosefta it concludes and writes and brings up in gentile courts because it is like saving from their hand — and literally in this language it is in Avodah Zarah daf 13 regarding going to a gentile fair, and Rashi explains it refers to courts that are permitted because it is like saving from their hand; and so explained in Maggid Mishneh chapter 9 Yom Tov, and Peri Megadim also brought this. And also in the Talmud on 13b that they weighed and discussed the reason implies this "like saving from their hand" does not refer to the essence of the permission to buy but only to the courts [however in Shach in the name of Rabbeinu Yonah it somewhat implies like his words here]. And therefore here too one must explain regarding writing and bringing up in courts that it is permitted on the festival because it is like saving from their hand. If so, another reason is needed for permission to buy from a gentile on Yom Tov. Indeed this very law in my humble opinion is not clear, for all the Rishonim did not copy this Tosefta at all, and since Rambam and all poskim omitted this Tosefta it appears they do not hold thus for halacha; and Rambam was silent and wrote the mishnah law that one does not buy houses, etc., only for festival need, and did not distinguish at all that from a gentile it is permitted to buy houses in any manner; and the reason one could say: since the mishnah was silent "one does not buy," etc., only for festival need and did not distinguish that from a gentile it is permitted, and so in the Talmud it did not bring this Tosefta to distinguish in this — evidently they do not hold thus for halacha; and more so since the mishnah specified only for festival need or for the seller's need — evidently we have no other manner of permission. And further one can say Rambam and Shulchan Aruch who did not write this permission explain the Tosefta with another explanation from Shach: the Tosefta did not come to innovate that from a gentile is more permitted than from an Israelite, but only that from a gentile is also permitted, and it also deals specifically with festival need and did not need to explain this since it refers to the mishnah and only added that from a gentile is also permitted; even though these matters need writing and bringing up in courts, nevertheless it is permitted, since buying is permitted for festival need, writing and courts are also permitted because it is like saving from their hand [and as explained from Rashi and Maggid Mishneh] [and were I not afraid I would also say the Tosefta does not refer at all to festival matters, for all the Tosefta's language was taught in Avodah Zarah daf 13 and Eruvin daf 47 regarding going to a gentile fair, and only these words "going to a gentile fair and buying," etc. are missing here and were taught here that the reason for permission is because it is like davar ha-aved that he will not find on another day [and in the preceding baraita it also deals with the festival regarding davar ha-aved], and as brought here in the Talmud daf 11 regarding davar ha-aved; and it is taught regarding idolatry similarly, see there and see in Avodah Zarah in Rosh and Ran in the name of Yerushalmi that all the permission is regarding idolatry because it is like davar ha-aved, for at the fair he finds opportunity to buy them — if so we have no Tosefta to permit here unless we say for this reason they also permitted on chol ha-moed to go to the fair and buy from them, for on another day perhaps he will not obtain them; but then Shach should have mentioned specifically fair]. Nevertheless regarding houses and fields in the Land of Israel perhaps one may be lenient because of settling the Land, but in the diaspora in my humble opinion this law is not clear at all.
